```sql
/*  Monthly outage‑episode report – one statement only  */
WITH
/* 1.  Remove skipped checks */
filtered AS (
    SELECT service, checked_at, status
    FROM checks
    WHERE status <> 'skipped'
),

/* 2.  Order checks per service and look at the previous row */
ordered AS (
    SELECT
        service,
        checked_at,
        status,
        LAG(status) OVER (PARTITION BY service ORDER BY checked_at)            AS prev_status,
        LAG(checked_at) OVER (PARTITION BY service ORDER BY checked_at)        AS prev_time
    FROM filtered
),

/* 3.  Flag the first row of every failing run (fail or timeout)  */
run_start_flag AS (
    SELECT
        service,
        checked_at,
        status,
        CASE
            WHEN status IN ('fail','timeout')
                 AND (prev_status NOT IN ('fail','timeout'))
            THEN 1 ELSE 0
        END                                                         AS is_run_start
    FROM ordered
),

/* 4.  Assign a run id – cumulative sum of run starts  */
run_id AS (
    SELECT
        service,
        checked_at,
        status,
        SUM(is_run_start) OVER (PARTITION BY service ORDER BY checked_at
                                ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)         AS run_id
    FROM run_start_flag
),

/* 5.  Aggregate data per run   */
runs AS (
    SELECT
        service,
        run_id,
        MIN(checked_at)                                                AS run_start_at,
        MAX(checked_at)                                                AS run_end_at,
        SUM(CASE WHEN status IN ('fail','timeout') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)   AS run_failed_checks,
        MAX(CASE WHEN status = 'ok' THEN checked_at END)              AS recovery_at,   -- NULL if no recovery
        MAX(CASE WHEN status IN ('fail','timeout') THEN checked_at END) AS last_fail_at
    FROM run_id
    GROUP BY service, run_id
),

/* 6.  Determine whether a run starts a new episode  */
episode_assign AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        CASE
            /* first run of the service always starts an episode */
            WHEN LAG(run_start_at) OVER (PARTITION BY service ORDER BY run_start_at) IS NULL
                 THEN 1
            /* start new episode if at least 10 min after previous recovery */
            WHEN run_start_at - LAG(recovery_at) OVER (PARTITION BY service ORDER BY run_start_at) >= 10
                 THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END                                                        AS new_episode_flag
    FROM runs
),

/* 7.  Assign an episode id – cumulative sum of new‑episode flags  */
episode_id AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        SUM(new_episode_flag) OVER (PARTITION BY service ORDER BY run_start_at
                                    ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)      AS episode_id
    FROM episode_assign
),

/* 8.  Aggregate data per episode   */
episode_agg AS (
    SELECT
        service,
        episode_id,
        MIN(run_start_at)                                                AS started_at,
        MAX(recovery_at)                                                 AS ended_at,      -- NULL if open
        CASE
            WHEN MAX(recovery_at) IS NOT NULL
                 THEN MAX(recovery_at) - MIN(run_start_at)               /* closed episode */
            ELSE MAX(last_fail_at) - MIN(run_start_at)                  /* open episode   */
        END                                                              AS duration_min,
        SUM(run_failed_checks)                                           AS failed_checks
    FROM episode_id
    GROUP BY service, episode_id
),

/* 9.  Keep only open episodes or those long enough (≥ 15 min)  */
filtered_episodes AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM episode_agg
    WHERE ended_at IS NULL OR duration_min >= 15
),

/* 10.  Rank the reported episodes by duration (desc), start time (asc)  */
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY service
                           ORDER BY duration_min DESC, started_at ASC) AS severity_rank
    FROM filtered_episodes
)

SELECT
    service,
    started_at,
    ended_at,
    duration_min,
    failed_checks,
    severity_rank
FROM ranked
ORDER BY service, started_at;
```

This query:

* removes all `skipped` rows,
* identifies maximal failing runs,
* chains runs into episodes when the next run starts less than 10 minutes after the previous run’s recovery,
* calculates `started_at`, `ended_at`, `duration_min`, and `failed_checks`,
* filters out short closed episodes (less than 15 minutes) while keeping all open episodes,
* ranks the reported episodes per service by duration (descending) and start time (ascending),
* and finally returns the required columns sorted by `service` and `started_at`.

All work is done with window functions and a few CTEs, avoiding any correlated sub‑queries and keeping the query fast even for tens of thousands of rows.
